title: A Hybrid Attention and Prioritized Replay Framework for Humanoid Robot Basketball Shooting
abstract: Humanoid robot basketball shooting is a challenging visuomotor task because it requires robust visual perception, efficient decision making, and stable control under sparsereward conditions. To address these issues, we propose an integrated reinforcement learning framework that combines a hybrid attention-based perception module with a PER-enhanced PSRSAC algorithm. In the perception stage, convolutional feature extraction is coupled with multi-head self-attention to capture both local visual details and global spatial relationships among the ball, basket, and robot body. In the decision stage, prioritized experience replay is incorporated into a multi-buffer replay structure, enabling more effective reuse of recent, successful, and informative transitions and thereby improving sample efficiency. Extensive simulation experiments are conducted on the Robotis OP2 humanoid robot in the Webots environment under fixed, random, and perturbed scenarios. The results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baseline reinforcement learning methods in terms of success rate, convergence speed, and robustness. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for complex sparse-reward visuomotor tasks and highlight its potential for humanoid robotic sports applications.

title: Contrastive Conformal Sets
abstract: Contrastive learning produces coherent semantic feature embeddings by encouraging positive samples to cluster closely while separating negative samples. However, existing contrastive learning methods lack a principled construction of geometric sets in the semantic feature space with distribution-free guarantees at any user-specified coverage level. We extend conformal prediction to this setting by introducing covering sets equipped with learnable generalized hyper-ball constraints. We propose a method that constructs conformal sets guaranteeing user-specified coverage of positive samples while maximizing negative sample exclusion. We theoretically motivate volume minimization as a proxy for negative exclusion, enabling our approach to operate effectively even when negative pairs are unavailable. The positive inclusion guarantee inherits the distribution-free coverage property of conformal prediction, while negative exclusion is maximized through learned set geometry optimized on a held-out training split. Experiments on simulated and real-world image datasets demonstrate improved inclusion-exclusion trade-offs compared to standard distance-based conformal baselines.

title: Distributed Quantum Discrete Logarithm Algorithm
abstract: Solving the discrete logarithm problem (DLP) with quantum computers is a fundamental task with important implications. Beyond Shor's algorithm, many researchers have proposed alternative solutions in recent years. However, due to current hardware limitations, the scale of DLP instances that can be addressed by quantum computers remains insufficient. To overcome this limitation, we propose a distributed quantum discrete logarithm algorithm that reduces the required quantum register size for solving DLPs. Specifically, we design a distributed quantum algorithm to determine whether the solution is contained in a given set. Based on this procedure, our method solves DLPs by identifying the intersection of sets containing the solution. Compared with Shor's original algorithm, our approach reduces the register size and can improve the success probability, while requiring no quantum communication.

title: Analisis Kinerja Deep Learning dalam Deteksi Dini Penyakit Menggunakan Citra Medis
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence technology, particularly deep learning, have been widely utilized in medical image processing to support early disease detection. Previous studies have shown that Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are capable of achieving high levels of accuracy in medical image classification, but differences in architecture and training methods result in varying performance. This study aims to analyze and compare the performance of deep learning algorithms in early disease detection using medical images, using previous research as a benchmark. Transfer learning-based CNN models, namely VGG16 and ResNet50, were used and evaluated using a labeled medical image dataset. Performance evaluation was conducted using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics, and the results were compared with accuracy achieved in previous studies using similar approaches. The analysis showed that the ResNet50 model achieved an accuracy of up to 95.3%, comparable to or better than several previous studies. These findings confirm that the choice of CNN architecture and training strategy significantly influences the performance of medical image-based early disease detection systems.

title: Reconciling Authorship and Artificial Intelligence: A Human Contribution Framework
abstract: As the applications of artificial intelligence continue to burgeon across every industry, it has created a crisis in copyright law. AI challenges the foundational assumption that authorship is distinctly a human title. While courts have historically adapted to new creative technologies, the recent rejection of copyright claims in Thaler v. Perlmutter and the Ninth Circuit’s ruling in Naruto v. Slater revealed a critical gap in the legal doctrine. Current U.S. law is unclear on what circumstances human and artificial intelligence collaboration satisfy the constitutional and statutory requirement of human-centered and originality. This paper argues that courts can and should recognize intellectual property rights for artificial intelligence assisted works that exhibit a spark of human creativity, without redefining authorship. It does this by taking account of historical precedence of seminal cases like Burrow-Giles Lithographic Co. v. Sarony and Feist Publications, Inc. v. Rural Telephone Service Co., and by comparing international approaches taken by China, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. The paper proposes a statutory Human Contribution test that requires three key elements, demonstrable creative direction, intellectual shaping of product, and an authorial intent to create said work. By clarifying the boundaries of authorship in AI-assisted work, this paper introduces a framework that resolves a pressing legal dilemma and ensures copyright law continues to incentivize human innovation, prevent market distortions, and fulfill its constitutional purpose to "promote the Progress of Science and useful Arts" in the age of artificial intelligence.

title: From AI to digital transformation
abstract: This chapter examines how organizations can move beyond the “AI experimentation trap” to achieve meaningful digital transformation. It explains what AI can and cannot do, explores its implications for jobs and skills, and outlines how AI drives value creation. The chapter emphasizes the need for an ecosystem approach, where automation, augmentation, and data are integrated strategically rather than pursued through isolated pilots. Drawing on the concept of generative AI, it shows how adaptability, scalability, and collaborative networks enable value creation but also introduce organizational and ethical challenges. Managers are urged to adopt a mutual shaping view of AI and organizations, recognizing AI&s;s dual role as a technical and strategic resource. The chapter concludes that overcoming cultural resistance, skill gaps, and weak strategic alignment is essential for turning AI-driven experimentation into sustained digital transformation and organizational value.

title: Graph-Based Deep Learning for Estrogen Receptor Status Classification in Breast Cancer Using H&E-stained Histology Images
abstract: This research improves breast cancer care by identifying estrogen receptor status, which shows the hormonal nature of the cancer and is essential for treatment decisions. It uses tissue images with routine haematoxylin and eosin staining, without relying on additional immunohistochemistry staining. The method learns visual patterns from these images and models how cancer cells are organised and connected using a new graph modelling strategy that improves machine learning accuracy. It introduces an ensemble approach, applied for the first time to estrogen receptor status classification, combining the high sensitivity of image-based models with the high specificity of graph-based models, enabling faster, more objective, and reliable diagnosis and better treatment planning.

title: AI Multimodal Personalized Language-Assisted Inclusive Early Childhood Education: Improving Early Reading and Classroom Interaction Ability of SEN Children
abstract: The support provided for children with Special Educational Needs (SEN) in mainstream early childhood language settings is not typically scalable or personalised. We design a novel Hybrid Edge-Cloud computational framework - Multimodal Personalized Language Support (MPLS) system - to address this decades old deficit. The system is based on Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) for accurate learner modelling and Contextual Bandit (CB) algorithms for adaptive activity sequencing. MPLS uses an Early Feature Fusion architecture based on a Multimodal Transformer that incorporates real-time sensory data including audio prosodics and kinesthetic features to dynamically adapt and match literacy activities (picture, audio and gesture-based) to complex learner profiles. We validate this system via a multi-site classroom-level quasi-experiment over 12 weeks across participating kindergartens. Data sources include pre-/post-tests of early literacy (vocabulary, phonological/morphological awareness, and oral comprehension), observation rubrics of engagement, system learning analytics, and teacher interviews. Learning gains are subsequently estimated via mixed-effects models with multimodal engagement scores tested as a mediator and language background/SEN type as moderators. This work goes the extra mile to provide: - A computationally rigorous DKT-CB framework - A validated Transformer-based fusion architecture for high-variance, low-signal inclusive setups, thus preserving pedagogical efficacy while promoting educational equity.

title: Enhanced Encrypted IoT Malicious Traffic Detection via Adaptive Fusion and Focal Loss: An Improved Heterogeneous Graph Approach
abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has significantly expanded the attack surface of network environments, making malicious traffic detection a critical security challenge. The widespread adoption of encryption technologies further exacerbates this challenge, as traditional plaintext feature-based detection methods are no longer effective. Although existing deep learning approaches have shown progress in encrypted traffic classification, they still face limitations in feature fusion strategies and the accurate identification of hard-to-classify samples. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes an enhanced approach based on a dual-granularity heterogeneous graph neural network framework. Specifically, we introduce an adaptive feature fusion mechanism that dynamically adjusts feature weights and employs cross-view attention to fully exploit the complementarity of features across different granularities. Additionally, we replace the conventional cross-entropy loss with Focal Loss, enabling the model to focus more on challenging MitM (Man-in-the-Middle) samples during training. Extensive experiments conducted on the CIC-IIoT 2025 and IoT-23 datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves significant improvements in both weighted average accuracy and F1 score over baseline methods. Compared to the state-of-the-art encrypted traffic classification framework, MH-Net, the F1 score improves by 11.5% on the CIC-IIoT dataset, while also significantly reducing the misclassification of MitM samples as benign traffic. These results confirm the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. This work provides a practical solution for encrypted traffic classification in IoT environments, enabling more accurate detection of malicious traffic and improving the security of IoT networks.

evidence.title: Enhanced Encrypted IoT Malicious Traffic Detection via Adaptive Fusion and Focal Loss: An Improved Heterogeneous Graph Approach
evidence.abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has significantly expanded the attack surface of network environments, making malicious traffic detection a critical security challenge. The widespread adoption of encryption technologies further exacerbates this challenge, as traditional plaintext feature-based detection methods are no longer effective. Although existing deep learning approaches have shown progress in encrypted traffic classification, they still face limitations in feature fusion strategies and the accurate identification of hard-to-classify samples. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes an enhanced approach based on a dual-granularity heterogeneous graph neural network framework. Specifically, we introduce an adaptive feature fusion mechanism that dynamically adjusts feature weights and employs cross-view attention to fully exploit the complementarity of features across different granularities. Additionally, we replace the conventional cross-entropy loss with Focal Loss, enabling the model to focus more on challenging MitM (Man-in-the-Middle) samples during training. Extensive experiments conducted on the CIC-IIoT 2025 and IoT-23 datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves significant improvements in both weighted average accuracy and F1 score over baseline methods. Compared to the state-of-the-art encrypted traffic classification framework, MH-Net, the F1 score improves by 11.5% on the CIC-IIoT dataset, while also significantly reducing the misclassification of MitM samples as benign traffic. These results confirm the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. This work provides a practical solution for encrypted traffic classification in IoT environments, enabling more accurate detection of malicious traffic and improving the security of IoT networks.

title: Trusted Framework Based on BMC Trusted Subsystem
abstract: The server has become the central part of the information society, which means that the stable operation of the server is essential for people. Hence, the trusted framework based on the BMC trusted subsystem is introduced in this paper. The Trusted Platform Module (TPM) and the Real Time Operating System (RTOS) in the BMC are regarded as the trusted root of the dual-core system of the BMC. The framework establishes a complete trust chain from server startup to program running under the OS according to the trusted root. The results indicate that the safety of the system operation is greatly improved because there is hardware isolation between protective parts, such as the trusted root and computing parts. Meanwhile, the trusted compute with the dual firmware containing the BIOS and the BMC ensures the safe startup of the server. Besides, the OS realizes the static and dynamic measurement for the executable files and running code based on the interaction with the trusted root through the TPM protocol family. Hence, the novel trusted framework can provide adequate security for the full operation cycle of the server.

title: Clawed and Dangerous: Can We Trust Open Agentic Systems?
abstract: Open agentic systems combine LLM-based planning with external capabilities, persistent memory, and privileged execution. They are used in coding assistants, browser copilots, and enterprise automation. OpenClaw is a visible instance of this broader class. Without much attention yet, their security challenge is fundamentally different from that of traditional software that relies on predictable execution and well-defined control flow. In open agentic systems, everything is ''probabilistic'': plans are generated at runtime, key decisions may be shaped by untrusted natural-language inputs and tool outputs, execution unfolds in uncertain environments, and actions are taken under authority delegated by human users. The central challenge is therefore not merely robustness against individual attacks, but the governance of agentic behavior under persistent uncertainty. This paper systematizes the area through a software engineering lens. We introduce a six-dimensional analytical taxonomy and synthesize 50 papers spanning attacks, benchmarks, defenses, audits, and adjacent engineering foundations. From this synthesis, we derive a reference doctrine for secure-by-construction agent platforms, together with an evaluation scorecard for assessing platform security posture. Our review shows that the literature is relatively mature in attack characterization and benchmark construction, but remains weak in deployment controls, operational governance, persistent-memory integrity, and capability revocation. These gaps define a concrete engineering agenda for building agent ecosystems that are governable, auditable, and resilient under compromise.

title: Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Network Security Across Healthcare Providers
abstract: Hackers are employing increasingly advanced methods to target hospital networks, electronic health data, medical IoT devices, and telemedicine apps as the healthcare industry becomes more digitally integrated.Gathering and sharing private medical information is essential when employing centralized machine learning to identify intrusions.Important concerns are privacy, regulations, and compliance with HIPAA, GDPR, and other laws.Federated Learning (FL) is an approach to learning that protects patient data and does not depend on a central server.It makes it possible for different healthcare facilities to work together to create efficient security models.This study looks at the ways that FL can enhance network security and preserve privacy in the healthcare industry.It explores secure aggregation techniques, federated learning systems, differential privacy strategies, and strong defences against inference and poisoning attacks.By using a hierarchical federated framework, this study shows how multi-provider healthcare organizations can increase detection accuracy while preserving their independence, privacy, and compliance.

title: Enhancing Sentiment Classification in Video Content Via CrossModel Attention on Text, Audio and Visual Modalities
abstract: Multi-modal sentiment analysis aims to understand human emotions by combining information from different data sources such as text, audio, and visual signals. However, many existing methods struggle to effectively capture and align these modalities, especially in video-based content where emotional cues are complex and interdependent. This paper proposes a unified framework for sentiment classification that integrates textual, acoustic, and visual features. The model uses BERT for text representation, ResNet for visual feature extraction, and Wav2Vec for audio processing. A crossmodal attention mechanism is applied to dynamically fuse information from all modalities, enabling better interaction and understanding between them. Experiments are conducted on the CMU-MOSEI dataset, A widely used benchmark for multi-modal sentiment analysis. The proposed approach is expected to improve classification accuracy compared to traditional uni-modal and simple fusion methods. The results demonstrate the importance of cross-modal interaction in capturing rich emotional context in real-world video data.
